questions.question: Fill in the blank: The % operator gives the ______ after division.

correct.title: Perfect! 🎉
correct.details: The modulus operator % returns the remainder of a division operation. For example, 7 % 2 equals 1.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The modulus operator % returns the remainder of a division operation. For example, 7 % 2 equals 1.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Functions make code ______ and organized.

correct.title: Perfect! 🎉
correct.details: Functions allow you to write code once and use it multiple times, reducing repetition and making code easier to maintain.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Functions allow you to write code once and use it multiple times, reducing repetition and making code easier to maintain.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: === checks for ______ equality (value and type).

correct.title: Perfect! 🎉
correct.details: Strict equality (===) requires both the value and data type to be the same. 5 === "5" is false because types differ.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Strict equality (===) requires both the value and data type to be the same. 5 === "5" is false because types differ.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Use ______ to send a value back from a function.

correct.title: Perfect! 🎉
correct.details: The return statement ends function execution and specifies the value to be returned to the function caller.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The return statement ends function execution and specifies the value to be returned to the function caller.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: x *= 3 means x = x ______ 3.

correct.title: Perfect! 🎉
correct.details: *= is the multiplication assignment operator. x *= 3 is equivalent to x = x * 3.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: *= is the multiplication assignment operator. x *= 3 is equivalent to x = x * 3.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Function ______ are placeholders for input values.

correct.title: Perfect! 🎉
correct.details: Parameters are the names listed in the function definition. Arguments are the actual values passed when calling the function.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Parameters are the names listed in the function definition. Arguments are the actual values passed when calling the function.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 5 + "5" results in ______.

correct.title: Perfect! 🎉
correct.details: When mixing numbers and strings with +, JavaScript converts the number to a string and concatenates them.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: When mixing numbers and strings with +, JavaScript converts the number to a string and concatenates them.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Arrow functions use the ______ symbol.

correct.title: Perfect! 🎉
correct.details: Arrow functions use => syntax. For example: const add = (a, b) => a + b;

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Arrow functions use => syntax. For example: const add = (a, b) => a + b;
